jobs.description:

Job Description

Position Summary

As our new Director, Audience Strategy, you will take on blended agency + client-facing role that incorporates business consulting, analytical depth, and cross-functional leadership.

Serving as a trusted advisor, you will connect client priorities to the right data capabilities (1P, 2P, 3P), technology, and strategy, to help drive measurable business outcomes.
Using your financial accumen and eye for detail you will ensure accurate revenue reporting, campaign pacing, and identify opportunities to grow audience targeting usage
Using your technical expertise and analytics skills you will support a talented team of analysts on segment creation, activation, manage operational issues, and collaborate on the development of new tools that improve the efficiency and effectiveness of our processes.
Leveraging your industry knowledge and leadership skills, you will work with internal product teams and vendors partners to grow our capabilities.

This position requires strong strategic thinking, relationship building and management, presentation, critical thinking, and problem-solving skills.

Key Responsibilities

Audience Strategy

Own the audience narrative for clients and align all work to business priorities and measurable outcomes.
Advise senior stakeholders using data-driven insights across audience strategy, testing, and optimization.
Translate complex signals and technical concepts into clear, actionable recommendations that build confidence with clients, partners, and internal leaders
Support development of client-facing deliverables including segment specifications, activation guides, and performance reports
Evolve and manage client data partnerships to ensure our audience offering stays ahead of customer needs

Audience Execution

Manage audience infrastructure including segment uploads, match rate optimization, and troubleshooting activation issues across DSPs, social platforms, and other endpoints
Maintain documentation of audience build processes, segment definitions, and activation requirements
Support audience modeling projects including clustering, lookalike modeling, propensity scoring, and behavioral segmentation in partnership with Advanced Analytics team
Willingness and ability to be “hands-on” as needed to step in, guide, or support deliverables.

Team Development

Mentor a talented team of 4+
Contribute to internal training materials and knowledge sharing sessions
Support recruitment efforts by participating in interviews and candidate evaluations
Provide technical guidance to junior team members and media planners on audience capabilities and data requirements

Continuous Learning & Innovation

Stay current on audience strategy best practices, emerging technologies, and privacy developments
Pilot new tools, techniques, and data sources to expand team capabilities
Document learnings and contribute to internal process improvements
Explore applications of AI/ML for audience development under senior guidance

Qualifications

Required Experience

7+ years of experience in audience strategy, data strategy, programmatic media, or marketing analytics within agency, brand, or martech environments
Experience managing a multi-million-dollar budget
1-3 years of people management experience
Demonstrated ability to independently execute complex audience projects from data analysis through activation
Direct hands-on experience building audience segments and managing campaign activation across multiple platforms
Proven ability to communicate technical concepts clearly to non-technical stakeholders

Core Competencies

Strong bias toward action with attention to detail and quality
Exceptional presentation and written communication skill
Ability to manage multiple concurrent projects with competing priorities
Works effectively across teams and builds productive relationships
Comfortable with ambiguity and changing priorities in a fast-paced environment

This is an active vacancy. We are currently hiring for this role and reviewing applications on an ongoing basis.

Expected Salary: $105,000 - $115,000

Generous paid time off with a minimum of 37 paid days off including vacation and monthly wellness days. We also have four-day long weekends, half-day summer Fridays, and meeting-free Friday afternoons year-round.
A flexible hybrid work model that works for you.
A focus on personal development with formal training opportunities, including mental health training and inclusion education for everyone.

jobs.title: Director Supply Chain Strategy
jobs.description:
As the global leader in high-speed connectivity, Ciena builds the critical infrastructure powering the AI era. We’re a technology company shaping the future of networking, guided by innovation, integrity, and collaboration. Through development opportunities, meaningful work, and flexibility, Ciena supports growth and well-being—on and off the job. Connect with a career that matters.

The Director, Global Supply Chain Strategy & Architecture
is responsible for defining the long-term strategy and future-state architecture of the global Supply Chain organization.

This leader will translate business growth objectives, product strategy, customer requirements, market dynamics, and external supply-chain trends into an integrated global supply chain strategy and future-state design. The role will define the strategic choices required across the supply chain network, manufacturing and partner ecosystem, capacity, resilience, inventory positioning, and critical capabilities
to ensure the Supply Chain is positioned to scale, respond, and perform as the business evolves.

The Director will serve as the architect and integrator of the end-to-end supply chain
, connecting functional strategies into a cohesive future-state direction, identifying structural and capability requirements, developing strategic scenarios, and establishing the multi-year roadmap required to prepare Supply Chain for future business needs.

Key Responsibilities

Global Supply Chain Strategy
Lead the development and ongoing evolution of the global, multi-year Supply Chain strategy, aligned with the corporate strategy and growth objectives.
Translate business, product, market, and customer strategies into implications for the future supply chain.
Define the strategic choices required across areas such as global footprint, capacity, sourcing, manufacturing, inventory, logistics, supply assurance, resilience, and partner strategy.
Identify the capabilities required to enable the supply chain to scale effectively while maintaining agility, competitiveness, and customer responsiveness.
Maintain an external perspective on geopolitical developments, industry trends, supply-market dynamics, manufacturing models, and emerging supply-chain practices.
Physical Strategic Roadmap & Prioritization
Develop and maintain an integrated 3-5 year Supply Chain strategic roadmap, translating strategy into clear priorities and strategic initiatives.
Establish the strategic rationale and expected business outcomes associated with major supply-chain investments.
Identify dependencies and trade-offs across major strategic initiatives and recommend priorities
Ensure functional strategies connect to a common end-to-end direction rather than developing independently.
Partner with functional leaders to translate the global strategy into actionable priorities within their respective organizations.
Facilitate leadership discussions and strategy sessions focused on major supply-chain choices and priorities.
Establish a regular cadence for reviewing the Supply Chain strategy, external assumptions, strategic risks, and progress against priorities.
Ensure strategic decisions are translated into clear ownership and accountability across the Supply Chain organization.
Supply Chain Network & Ecosystem Strategy
Develop strategic perspectives on the global supply-chain footprint and ecosystem required to support future growth.
Assess long-term requirements for manufacturing capacity, geographic diversification, supplier ecosystem, contract manufacturing, distribution, and logistics networks.
Evaluate strategic make/buy/partner considerations and recommend the appropriate operating model for different elements of the supply chain.
Incorporate geopolitical, concentration, continuity, capacity, cost, and customer considerations into global network decisions.
Partner with functional leaders to develop strategies that strengthen supply assurance and reduce structural supply-chain risk.
Strategic Capacity & Scale Readiness
Assess the supply chain's ability to support future revenue, product, volume, and customer requirements.
Identify structural constraints that could limit the company's ability to scale.
Develop strategic scenarios for different growth, demand, supply, and geopolitical conditions.
Identify where additional capacity, capability, supplier diversification, inventory, or ecosystem investment may be required.
Establish a forward-looking view of supply-chain readiness and bring recommended actions and trade-offs to senior leadership.
Strategic Business & Financial Analysis
Develop fact-based recommendations for complex supply-chain decisions, clearly articulating options, trade-offs, risks, investment requirements, and expected business outcomes.
Develop business cases for significant strategic supply-chain investments and decisions.
Partner with Finance to assess the financial implications of alternative supply-chain strategies.
Balance service, growth, resilience, inventory, working capital, cost, and investment considerations when developing strategic recommendations.
Establish measures that demonstrate whether the supply-chain strategy is delivering the intended business outcomes.
Enterprise & Cross-Functional Alignment
Build strong partnerships across Product Line Management (PLM), R&D, Finance, Sales Operations, and other Enterprise functions.
Connect product roadmaps, business growth plans, financial objectives, and customer requirements to future supply-chain requirements.
Ensure Supply Chain implications are incorporated early into major business and product decisions.

Outside the Scope of This Role

This Role Does Not Own

Digital supply-chain strategy or technology implementation
Process transformation and process redesign
Supply-chain systems implementation
Automation or AI deployment
Transformation program management
Day-to-day functional or operational execution

The Must Haves

Bachelor’s degree in supply chain, Operations, Engineering, Business, Finance, or a related discipline.
Significant progressive experience in global supply chain, operations, strategy, or a related leadership role.
Broad end-to-end understanding of supply-chain disciplines including planning, sourcing, manufacturing, inventory, logistics, supplier management, and supply assurance.
Demonstrated ability to develop long-term strategy and translate complex business requirements into clear strategic priorities.
Experience within a complex global manufacturing environment, ideally technology, telecommunications, electronics, semiconductor, or a related sector.
Experience evaluating supply-chain networks, manufacturing strategies, capacity requirements, outsourcing models, and/or global supply ecosystems.
Strong business and financial acumen with experience developing investment recommendations and evaluating strategic trade-offs.
Exceptional executive communication skills and demonstrated ability to influence senior stakeholders across organizational boundaries.

Nice To Have

MBA or advanced degree in Supply Chain, Operations, Engineering, Finance, or related discipline.
Experience working within an outsourced or contract-manufacturing operating model.
Experience supporting periods of significant business growth or structural change.
Experience with scenario planning, network strategy, supply-chain risk, and global capacity strategy.

Leadership Competencies

Enterprise Thinking: Optimizes decisions for the end-to-end business rather than individual functions.
Strategic Foresight: Anticipates future business requirements and their implications for the supply chain.
Commercial Acumen: Connects supply-chain choices directly to growth, customers and financial outcomes.
Structured Problem Solving: Brings clarity and fact-based thinking to ambiguous strategic issues.
Influence & Alignment: Builds commitment across functions and senior leaders.
Executive Presence: Communicates complex strategic issues simply and confidently.
Decision Orientation: Moves strategy beyond analysis into clear choices, priorities, and accountability.

Pay Ranges

The salary range for this role in Ottawa, Canada is $144, 900 - $231, 500

The salary range for this role in the eastern-USA is $158, 800 - $253, 600

Pay ranges at Ciena are designed to accommodate variations in knowledge, skills, experience, market conditions, and locations, reflecting our diverse products, industries, and lines of business. Please note that the pay range information provided in this posting pertains specifically to the primary location, which is the top location listed in case multiple locations are available.

Non-Sales employees may be eligible for a discretionary incentive bonus, while Sales employees may be eligible for a sales commission. In addition to competitive compensation, Ciena offers a comprehensive benefits package, including medical, dental, and vision plans, participation in 401(K) (USA) & DCPP (Canada) with company matching, Employee Stock Purchase Program (ESPP), Employee Assistance Program (EAP), company-paid holidays, paid sick leave, and vacation time. We also comply with all applicable laws regarding Paid Family Leave and other leaves of absence.

At Ciena, we are committed to building and fostering an environment in which our employees feel respected, valued, and heard. Ciena values the diversity of its workforce and respects its employees as individuals. We do not tolerate any form of discrimination.

Ciena is an Equal Opportunity Employer, including disability and protected veteran status.

If contacted in relation to a job opportunity, please advise Ciena of any accommodation measures you may require.

jobs.title: DIRECTOR OF INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
jobs.description:
About The Lacroix Medical Group

A leader in private medicine in Quebec, the Lacroix Medical Group comprises three rapidly growing divisions:

Medical Clinics
Operating Rooms
Biomedical Laboratory

The organization has experienced strong and sustained growth since its founding in 2009 and currently employs nearly 350 people. As part of its strategic plan, the Group aims to accelerate its national and international development.

OUR MISSION

To be the benchmark in private healthcare.

OUR VALUES

Passion | Respect | Integrity | Commitment | Innovation.

The Mandate

In a context of sustained growth and transformation of its activities, Lacroix Medical Group is seeking a Director of Information Technology who will actively contribute to the organization's technological evolution.

Reporting directly to the President and CEO, the Director of IT plays a strategic role across the entire network. They are responsible for defining, structuring, and developing the IT function to effectively support the organization's operations, growth, and ambitions.

They provide leadership for technology strategy, infrastructure, business systems, cybersecurity, data governance, digital transformation, and artificial intelligence.

He is also responsible for the performance of his team and the organization's technology partner ecosystem. This role is for an experienced, business-oriented, and results-driven IT leader who can combine strategic vision with excellent execution. Your Key Responsibilities IT Strategy and Governance: Define and deploy the IT vision and master plan in line with the strategic, operational, and financial priorities of Groupe médical Lacroix. Advise senior management on investments, risks, and key technological choices.

Performance and Business Continuity

Ensure the performance, robustness, and high availability of the infrastructure and technology platforms essential to the network's medical and administrative activities, including ERP, CRM, DME, LIS, SaaS, and cloud environments.

Digital Transformation, Data, and Artificial Intelligence

Identify and prioritize initiatives to transform the organization through technology, data valorization, automation, and artificial intelligence. Lead major technology projects and ensure their effective integration into operations.

Cybersecurity and Risk Management

Maintain high standards in cybersecurity, information protection, redundancy, and business continuity in an environment where system availability and the protection of medical data are critical.

Leadership and Organizational Performance

Lead and develop a competent, autonomous, and accountable IT team. Establish clear objectives and performance indicators, ensure rigorous budget management, and optimize the contribution of suppliers, consultants, and technology partners.

An Executive Role Close to Operations

At Lacroix Medical Group, technology must meet the realities on the ground.

The IT Director will therefore need to maintain close contact with the various business units and network teams to understand their needs, anticipate challenges, and ensure that technological solutions contribute concretely to operational performance and service quality.

The position consequently requires excellent mobility. The successful candidate will be required to travel regularly throughout the Lacroix network in Quebec to meet with teams, support projects, and remain connected to the operational realities of the various facilities.

This on-the-ground presence is an essential component of the role and not an occasional responsibility.

The mandate expressly includes regular visits to service points.

The Ideal Candidate

We are looking for an experienced manager with a strong business acumen and excellent technological expertise, recognized for their leadership, judgment, and ability to drive organizational growth.

The Ideal Candidate Will Possess

A bachelor's degree in computer engineering, computer science, or a related field;
15 to 20 years of experience in information technology, including a minimum of 5 years in a management role;
Mastery of software architecture and project management;
A solid understanding of multi-site and cloud infrastructures;
Good knowledge of SaaS environments and major business platforms: ERP, CRM, financial systems, telephony, Microsoft 365, and others;
A thorough understanding of the issues cybersecurity, data governance and valorization, and artificial intelligence;
Proven experience in team management and development;
Recognized leadership in transformation and change management;
Ability to prioritize, make decisions, and manage effectively in a complex and evolving environment;
Excellent business acumen and the ability to communicate technological issues to senior management;
Fluency in French and English, both written and spoken;
A valid driver's license, a vehicle, and significant availability for regular travel throughout the network.

The Leader Profile We Are Looking For

Beyond technological expertise, we are looking for someone who stands out for their ability to mobilize, structure, and deliver.

A positive and committed leader with a strong sense of Accountability, the ability to build high-performing teams, manage rigorously, challenge the status quo, and transform technological challenges into concrete solutions for the business. The IT Director must be equally comfortable discussing strategy with senior management and understanding the challenges faced by teams in the field. Conditions and Compensation Lacroix Medical Group offers a competitive total compensation package including: Annual salary of $140,000 to $175,000, depending on experience and expertise; 4 weeks of vacation and 4 paid personal days; RRSP+ program with employer contribution; Cell phone allowance; Lacroix Health Credit; and an annual Lacroix gift card. This benefit can be combined with other benefits for personalized medical services.

Business travel expense account for trips outside your usual work area

Join a growing network and become a key player in the future of private medicine in Quebec.

Apply now and make a real difference.

jobs.title: Director, Governance and Controls
jobs.description:
Are you looking for a leadership role where you can shape how an organization operates, manages risk, and achieves excellence? Can you see yourself driving enterprise-wide governance, performance, and continuous improvement initiatives that support safe, secure, and efficient operations? If you answered yes, this may be the job for you. Apply today
! Our Chalk River location is looking for a Director, Governance and Controls
to provide strategic leadership for CNL's management system, governance frameworks, safeguards management, nuclear material accountability, human performance, and organizational effectiveness programs.

What you will be doing!

Leadership and Strategic Direction
Developing and implementing the strategic vision, objectives and performance expectations for the Governance and Controls organization.
Establishing long-term plans supporting corporate objectives and operational priorities.
Providing leadership for enterprise-wide Governance and Controls initiatives.
Promoting a culture of accountability, continuous learning, and operational discipline.
Aligning departmental objectives with corporate strategic priorities.
Ensuring programs and initiatives support CNL contractual commitments and business objectives.
Advising executives on organizational performance risks, opportunities and strategic considerations.
Championing safety, security, quality and environmental stewardship principles throughout the organization.

Management Systems and Compliance
Providing executive oversight of Management System and Nuclear Materials & Safeguard Management Functional Support Areas (FSA).
Establishing governance frameworks that support corporate accountability and compliance objectives.
Ensuring CNL’s management system remains compliant with CNSC licence requirements, AECL contractual obligations, CSA standards and corporate policies.
Directing development, implementation and maintenance of corporate governance processes.
Monitoring management system effectiveness and identifying opportunities for improvement.
Leading evaluations of governance performance and compliance effectiveness.
Overseeing corporate procedure development standards and governance requirements.
Supporting regulatory inspections, audits and assessments.
Directing corrective action programs related to governance and management system deficiencies.
Ensuring management system documentation remains current and aligned with operational requirements.
Acting as a senior authority for governance-related decisions and compliance matters.

Operational Integration and Resource Management
Ensuring the integration of Management System and Nuclear Materials and Safeguards activities across multiple sites and organizations.
Overseeing departmental budgets, forecasts and financial performance.
Directing workforce planning and resource allocation activities.
Supporting development of annual business plans and performance objectives.
Ensuring contractual commitments and deliverables are achieved.
Monitoring program performance against established plans.

Performance Improvement and Stakeholder Engagement
Providing organizational performance updates to governance committees.
Supporting executive decision-making through analysis and recommendations.
Interfacing with regulators, customers, and oversight organizations.
Participating in senior management committees and review boards.
Representing CNL during external assessments, inspections and audits.
Responding to executive and regulatory information requests.
Communicating strategic priorities and organizational expectations.
Promoting stakeholder confidence in organizational performance.

People Leadership and Organizational Capability
Leading, coaching and developing professional, technical and managerial staff.
Establishing performance objectives and accountability expectations.
Conducting performance management and talent development activities.
Supporting succession planning and workforce sustainability initiatives.
Supporting organizational change management initiatives.
Ensuring personnel possess required qualifications and competencies.

Other duties as assigned by your manager.

What We Are Looking For

Education
Bachelor's degree in business administration, engineering, science, quality management, organizational effectiveness, public administration, or a related discipline.
Master's degree considered an asset.
Professional certifications in governance, quality management, auditing, risk management, organizational effectiveness, or change management are considered assets.

Experience
Minimum 10 years of progressively responsible leadership experience in a highly regulated environment with responsibility for governance, management systems, compliance, performance assurance, safeguards, quality, organizational effectiveness, or related functions.

Knowledge, Skills & Abilities
Ability to develop and execute strategic plans that align organizational priorities with corporate objectives while providing leadership in governance, management systems, regulatory compliance, and risk management.
Ability to drive organizational effectiveness, performance improvement, and continuous improvement initiatives, supported by strong financial and resource management expertise.
Exceptional executive communication, presentation, stakeholder engagement, and influencing skills, with the ability to build consensus and foster productive relationships across diverse groups.
Skilled in leading organizational change, making sound decisions in complex and highly regulated environments, and applying effective negotiation, facilitation, and conflict resolution techniques to achieve business objectives and resolve competing priorities.
Knowledge of Nuclear management system, Quality Assurance, nuclear regulatory environment, Functional Support Areas, safeguards and non-proliferation is an asset.

Security Clearance Eligibility Required
Level 2 Secret requires a minimum of 7 years of verifiable history in Canada, Australia, New Zealand, the United States, and/or the United Kingdom. CNL implements security screening in accordance with the Treasury Board of Canada Secretariat's “Standard on Security Screening” and the “Policy on Government Security.”

Working Conditions

Working schedule: Five (5) days per week, seven and a half (7.5) hours per day for a thirty-seven and a half (37.5) hour work week.
May be required to respond to emergent regulatory, operational, audit, or performance issues outside normal business hours.
Periodic travel to CNL and external sites is required, along with occasional extended workdays and after-hours availability to support business, operational, and regulatory requirements.

Why CNL?

Does the idea of working with a dynamic team across Canada to advance nuclear science and technology for a clean and secure world
excite you? At CNL, we’re reinventing ourselves to be industry leaders— pioneering solutions to the problems that matter most
.

From building the next generation of clean nuclear and hydrogen energy technologies
, to developing targeted cancer treatments
, to continuing our global leadership in environmental remediation
—we are driven by impact, innovation, and purpose.

What We Offer: A Total Rewards Package

We believe in taking care of our people. Here’s what you can expect as part of our team:

Paid time off: vacation, sick, personal, and floater days
Benefits effective Day One – no waiting period
Tuition support to help you keep learning and growing
A defined-benefit pension plan or a defined-contribution pension plan, depending on your employee group, to support your long‑term financial security

Do Our Priorities Resonate with You?

Delivering clean energy for today and tomorrow
Restoring and protecting the environment
Contributing to the health of Canadians

If so, you’ll feel right at home at CNL!

Location: Onsite

Located in the heart of the Ottawa Valley,
our Chalk River site offers a beautiful natural setting with forests, lakes, and wildlife
, right at your doorstep. Surrounded by welcoming communities such as Deep River, Petawawa, and Pembroke
, you’ll have access to unparalleled outdoor adventures
and a fantastic work-life balance
.

Please note:
This is a fully on-site position based at our Chalk River Laboratory in
Ontario.

Our Commitment to Equity, Diversity & Inclusion

At CNL, we are committed to fostering an environment that promotes equity, diversity, and inclusion
. We celebrate and welcome employees, stakeholders, and partners of all backgrounds and identities. Click here to read all about it!

We are proud to uphold a workplace culture grounded in our Core Values
:

new_jobs.title: Director Supply Chain Strategy
new_jobs.description:
As the global leader in high-speed connectivity, Ciena builds the critical infrastructure powering the AI era. We’re a technology company shaping the future of networking, guided by innovation, integrity, and collaboration. Through development opportunities, meaningful work, and flexibility, Ciena supports growth and well-being—on and off the job. Connect with a career that matters.

The Director, Global Supply Chain Strategy & Architecture
is responsible for defining the long-term strategy and future-state architecture of the global Supply Chain organization.

This leader will translate business growth objectives, product strategy, customer requirements, market dynamics, and external supply-chain trends into an integrated global supply chain strategy and future-state design. The role will define the strategic choices required across the supply chain network, manufacturing and partner ecosystem, capacity, resilience, inventory positioning, and critical capabilities
to ensure the Supply Chain is positioned to scale, respond, and perform as the business evolves.

The Director will serve as the architect and integrator of the end-to-end supply chain
, connecting functional strategies into a cohesive future-state direction, identifying structural and capability requirements, developing strategic scenarios, and establishing the multi-year roadmap required to prepare Supply Chain for future business needs.

Key Responsibilities

Global Supply Chain Strategy
Lead the development and ongoing evolution of the global, multi-year Supply Chain strategy, aligned with the corporate strategy and growth objectives.
Translate business, product, market, and customer strategies into implications for the future supply chain.
Define the strategic choices required across areas such as global footprint, capacity, sourcing, manufacturing, inventory, logistics, supply assurance, resilience, and partner strategy.
Identify the capabilities required to enable the supply chain to scale effectively while maintaining agility, competitiveness, and customer responsiveness.
Maintain an external perspective on geopolitical developments, industry trends, supply-market dynamics, manufacturing models, and emerging supply-chain practices.
Physical Strategic Roadmap & Prioritization
Develop and maintain an integrated 3-5 year Supply Chain strategic roadmap, translating strategy into clear priorities and strategic initiatives.
Establish the strategic rationale and expected business outcomes associated with major supply-chain investments.
Identify dependencies and trade-offs across major strategic initiatives and recommend priorities
Ensure functional strategies connect to a common end-to-end direction rather than developing independently.
Partner with functional leaders to translate the global strategy into actionable priorities within their respective organizations.
Facilitate leadership discussions and strategy sessions focused on major supply-chain choices and priorities.
Establish a regular cadence for reviewing the Supply Chain strategy, external assumptions, strategic risks, and progress against priorities.
Ensure strategic decisions are translated into clear ownership and accountability across the Supply Chain organization.
Supply Chain Network & Ecosystem Strategy
Develop strategic perspectives on the global supply-chain footprint and ecosystem required to support future growth.
Assess long-term requirements for manufacturing capacity, geographic diversification, supplier ecosystem, contract manufacturing, distribution, and logistics networks.
Evaluate strategic make/buy/partner considerations and recommend the appropriate operating model for different elements of the supply chain.
Incorporate geopolitical, concentration, continuity, capacity, cost, and customer considerations into global network decisions.
Partner with functional leaders to develop strategies that strengthen supply assurance and reduce structural supply-chain risk.
Strategic Capacity & Scale Readiness
Assess the supply chain's ability to support future revenue, product, volume, and customer requirements.
Identify structural constraints that could limit the company's ability to scale.
Develop strategic scenarios for different growth, demand, supply, and geopolitical conditions.
Identify where additional capacity, capability, supplier diversification, inventory, or ecosystem investment may be required.
Establish a forward-looking view of supply-chain readiness and bring recommended actions and trade-offs to senior leadership.
Strategic Business & Financial Analysis
Develop fact-based recommendations for complex supply-chain decisions, clearly articulating options, trade-offs, risks, investment requirements, and expected business outcomes.
Develop business cases for significant strategic supply-chain investments and decisions.
Partner with Finance to assess the financial implications of alternative supply-chain strategies.
Balance service, growth, resilience, inventory, working capital, cost, and investment considerations when developing strategic recommendations.
Establish measures that demonstrate whether the supply-chain strategy is delivering the intended business outcomes.
Enterprise & Cross-Functional Alignment
Build strong partnerships across Product Line Management (PLM), R&D, Finance, Sales Operations, and other Enterprise functions.
Connect product roadmaps, business growth plans, financial objectives, and customer requirements to future supply-chain requirements.
Ensure Supply Chain implications are incorporated early into major business and product decisions.

Outside the Scope of This Role

This Role Does Not Own

Digital supply-chain strategy or technology implementation
Process transformation and process redesign
Supply-chain systems implementation
Automation or AI deployment
Transformation program management
Day-to-day functional or operational execution

The Must Haves

Bachelor’s degree in supply chain, Operations, Engineering, Business, Finance, or a related discipline.
Significant progressive experience in global supply chain, operations, strategy, or a related leadership role.
Broad end-to-end understanding of supply-chain disciplines including planning, sourcing, manufacturing, inventory, logistics, supplier management, and supply assurance.
Demonstrated ability to develop long-term strategy and translate complex business requirements into clear strategic priorities.
Experience within a complex global manufacturing environment, ideally technology, telecommunications, electronics, semiconductor, or a related sector.
Experience evaluating supply-chain networks, manufacturing strategies, capacity requirements, outsourcing models, and/or global supply ecosystems.
Strong business and financial acumen with experience developing investment recommendations and evaluating strategic trade-offs.
Exceptional executive communication skills and demonstrated ability to influence senior stakeholders across organizational boundaries.

Nice To Have

MBA or advanced degree in Supply Chain, Operations, Engineering, Finance, or related discipline.
Experience working within an outsourced or contract-manufacturing operating model.
Experience supporting periods of significant business growth or structural change.
Experience with scenario planning, network strategy, supply-chain risk, and global capacity strategy.

Leadership Competencies

Enterprise Thinking: Optimizes decisions for the end-to-end business rather than individual functions.
Strategic Foresight: Anticipates future business requirements and their implications for the supply chain.
Commercial Acumen: Connects supply-chain choices directly to growth, customers and financial outcomes.
Structured Problem Solving: Brings clarity and fact-based thinking to ambiguous strategic issues.
Influence & Alignment: Builds commitment across functions and senior leaders.
Executive Presence: Communicates complex strategic issues simply and confidently.
Decision Orientation: Moves strategy beyond analysis into clear choices, priorities, and accountability.

Start leveraging 360Learning's partner and alliances ecosystem to accelerate new logo acquisition
Begin to achieve world class performance and hit quarterly targets
